title: Bhukailash Rajbari
description: You would not expect to find a grand old rajbari in the middle of Kidderpore, but Bhukailash Rajbari is still standing here with centuries of history behind it.

title: Clive House
description: This old house in Dum Dum is easy to miss, but it is believed to be one of the oldest colonial buildings still standing in Kolkata.

title: Armenian Church of the Holy Nazareth
description: Hidden inside the busy old city is a church built by Kolkata’s Armenian community, which was here even before the British.

title: Beth El Synagogue
description: Right around Kolkata’s busy trading streets is this beautiful synagogue that tells the story of the city’s once-thriving Jewish community.

title: Magen David Synagogue
description: I had passed through this area many times before realising that one of Kolkata’s most striking old synagogues was right here.

title: Chitreswari Kali Temple
description: This old Kali temple in Chitpur comes with a story you do not hear every day—dacoits are said to have prayed here before going on raids.

title: Cossipore Udyanbati
description: This peaceful garden house in Cossipore is where Sri Ramakrishna spent the last few months of his life.

title: Tiretta Bazaar Chinese Breakfast Market
description: Come here early enough and you will find one of Kolkata’s most special breakfasts—dumplings, buns and other Chinese favourites being sold before the city fully wakes up.

title: Kumartuli Idol-Makers’ Workshops
description: Walk into the smaller lanes of Kumartuli and you can actually see bamboo, straw and clay slowly taking the form of the idols we see during Puja.

title: Ahiritola Ghat
description: This is one of those ghats that feels like old Kolkata is still alive — people come here every day for rituals.
